From exabyte-scale knowledge indexes to codegen-first agent runtimes, the building blocks behind Perplexity's applications are some of the most battle-tested AI systems in the industry. We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. It's one thing to solve planet-scale retrieval, long-horizon orchestration, and other foundational AI challenges within a single product ecosystem. The true measure of success is to turn those solutions into elegant APIs that delight developers and agents alike. Our API Platform delivers frontier intelligence to thousands of customers: startups, trillion-dollar enterprises, U.S. and allied governments, and everyone in between. We've achieved incredible scale, yet we're just getting started. Join us to build tools for curious minds. ABOUT THIS ROLE Perplexity is seeking strong engineers with a passion for delivering frontier intelligence and infrastructure to developers. Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces. As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.). KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence. - Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services. - Build the paved road for API services: standardized service scaffolding, container builds, CI/CD, Kubernetes and Helm deployment, and progressive rollouts with fast rollback, so a new API product goes from idea to production in days, not weeks. - Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth. - Unify cross-cutting capabilities (billing and usage, rate limiting, organization and identity settings, analytics and observability) so every API product gets them by default instead of rebuilding them. - Ensure low latency and high throughput through aggressive performance optimization (including on upstream systems). - Harden system security and reliability across heterogeneous compute environments, and operate what you build: SLOs, on-call, and incident response. - Collaborate across teams to bring novel frontier capabilities into the API Platform, and partner with infrastructure teams on compute, networking, secrets, and security. - Continually reimagine the customer needs of tomorrow (and the architectures to serve those needs), while faithfully serving the customer workloads of today. - Uphold engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, and internal documentation. QUALIFICATIONS - 5+ years of backend engineering experience with Python, Go, or Rust, including significant time building platforms or infrastructure used by other engineering teams. - Strong understanding of high-traffic API design: schema evolution & versioning, idempotency, authentication patterns, rate limiting, and performance tuning. - Hands-on experience building and operating API gateways, reverse proxies, or routing layers: authentication and authorization, rate limiting and quotas, request routing, traffic shaping, and per-request observability. - Experience building API governance tooling: contract-first API design, breaking-change detection and API linting in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from the contract. - Platform depth across the build and deploy path: you have owned CI/CD pipelines, container builds and base images, infrastructure as code, and progressive delivery (canary or blue-green) on a major cloud. - A track record of owning a platform end to end: identifying the need, designing it, aligning the teams that depend on it, shipping it, and operating it, while raising the engineering bar for the teams building on it. - Strong customer empathy and product sense, ensuring the APIs you build are ergonomic, well-documented, and easy to adopt for developers and agents alike. Strong plus: - Experience with modern AI APIs (including latency tuning, streaming, model orchestration, emerging technical standards). - Usage-based billing and metering systems, multi-tenant organization and identity models, and usage analytics pipelines. - Observability for API platforms: structured logging pipelines, metrics, tracing, and SLO tooling.

items.title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Equipment
items.description: About the Team OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network. We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service. About the Role As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer, you will oversee the quality of data center equipment at supplier factories. You will use production data, audits, and test results to identify systemic, recurring, or safety-related issues and work with suppliers to address them through Closed Loop Learning (CLL). You will work with suppliers and internal teams to define inspections and factory tests for each type of equipment. You will coordinate issue resolution before shipment and manage deviations across multiple suppliers and project sites. Key Responsibilities Manufacturing Monitoring and Supplier Improvement - Manufacturing monitoring: Work with Manufacturing Operations to monitor production progress, quality controls, inspection results, and test readiness. Flag emerging risks and coordinate a response with suppliers. - Product and process audits: Audit products and processes during and after production against engineering requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure. - Manufacturing coordination: Agree on production checkpoints and inspection and testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery. - Manufacturing scorecards: Develop supplier and product scorecards with Manufacturing Operations. Review audit findings, test results, recurring defects, and open issues with suppliers to prioritize improvements. - Drive continuous improvement: Lead the CLL process with suppliers. Track root cause analyses and corrective and preventive actions in a shared register. Verify that each action addresses the underlying problem before closing it. Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) - Standardize requirements and formats: Develop product-specific FAT requirements and standard test formats with equipment suppliers and OpenAI’s engineering, commissioning, quality, and Manufacturing Operations teams. - Define critical quality requirements: Document the CTQ characteristics each test must verify in an OpenAI-accepted format. Use CLL findings to revise FAT procedures so future tests check for known failure modes. - Ensure auditable supplier records: Require suppliers to retain test results and make them available for OpenAI audits. - Manage documentation and revision control: Review final FAT records and audit reports for each piece of equipment and maintain a controlled revision history. - Conduct periodic supplier audits: Check that suppliers follow approved test procedures and that their records accurately reflect the tests performed. Factory Witness Testing (FWT) - Align checklists and stakeholders: Develop standard FWT checklists with OpenAI subject matter experts, installing contractors, and the construction management team. Agree on requirements before testing begins. - Manage documentation and reporting: Collect and review final witness test reports and supporting records from participants. - Before shipment, confirm that each witness-test issue is resolved or covered by a documented deviation. Log systemic, recurring, or safety-related findings in the CLL tracker and verify the effectiveness of corrective actions with the supplier. Deviation Management - Assess short shipments and missing or failed tests in partnership with Manufacturing Operations. - Coordinate supplier support to resolve issues at the project site. - Document each deviation and track the agreed actions through closure. Qualifications - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering. - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and project management. - Experience coordinating FAT and FWT with suppliers and resolving equipment quality issues. - Ability to develop test checklists, define CTQs, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records. - Experience monitoring supplier production, auditing products and processes during and after production, and using scorecards to improve supplier and product quality. Experience managing controlled documents and deviations. - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple pieces of equipment. - Ability to communicate quality requirements and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, and construction teams. - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40–60% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites. Preferred Skills - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems. - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities. - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor. - PMP or equivalent project management certification. - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments. This role focuses on strong advisory judgment and practical experience applying information reporting and withholding rules in fast-moving business environments. items.description: Perplexity AI is looking for a highly organized and resourceful IP Paralegal to serve as the operational backbone of a fast-growing, full-stack intellectual property program, with a primary responsibility for patent and trademark prosecution and portfolio management, and additional support work across copyrights, trade secrets, and open source compliance. This role reports to the Director of Intellectual Property and offers significant responsibility and direct exposure to novel questions at the intersection of artificial intelligence and IP law, as well as growth potential across other areas of an in-house practice group. You will partner closely with outside counsel, engineering stakeholders, and cross-functional teams to run the workflows behind a growing patent and trademark portfolio, maintain copyright and trade secret practices, and support open source compliance review. You will own day-to-day docketing and portfolio hygiene, manage outside counsel requests and billing against budget, and run intake and matter tracking so that nothing slips. You will also run our patent rewards program end-to-end and be a go-to resource for IP diligence support and IP-adjacent needs, including commercial and litigation support as needed. This role requires a genuine curiosity about using agentic AI systems to make the IP program run faster and more consistently, rather than treating AI tooling as an afterthought. This is a hands-on role for someone who is detail-obsessed, comfortable moving across multiple IP disciplines in the same week, fluent with AI and legal-technology tooling, and energized by building repeatable systems from the ground up so that a lean team can run a large, technically complex portfolio. If you are a curious person and your instinct when something breaks is to redesign the process, you will do well here. Key Responsibilities - Manage end-to-end workflows across the patent and trademark portfolios, including docketing, deadline tracking, filing coordination, portfolio maintenance, and status reporting to internal stakeholders. - Support trade secret protection practices and open source compliance review, including tracking disclosure and license obligations and flagging issues for attorney review. - Administer copyright matters, including registration filings, recordation, and portfolio record keeping. - Own intake and triage for new invention disclosures, trademark clearance requests, and other IP matters. - Manage outside counsel relationships and billing, including matter budgets, accrual tracking, invoice review against outside counsel guidelines, rate negotiation support, and matter-management hygiene in billing systems. - Run the patent rewards program. - Prepare and file U.S. trademark applications and coordinate foreign filings through local counsel. - Run preliminary clearance searches for new products and features. - Coordinate trademark office action responses, review watch notices, and recommend enforcement actions. - Manage the domain name portfolio and the online brand protection and takedown programs. - Conduct IP portfolio analysis, including filing trend tracking, competitive landscape monitoring, and gap identification, to support portfolio strategy and prosecution priorities. - Provide support on IP-adjacent matters as needed, including commercial contract IP terms and litigation support (e.g., document gathering, chronologies, and coordination with outside counsel). - Maintain and improve internal file management systems, trackers, and dashboards, keeping matter data, deadlines, and portfolio status current and audit-ready. - Build and improve the systems behind the work, including intake workflows, filing playbooks, matter templates, and escalation paths, so that recurring problems are solved structurally rather than absorbed by heroics. - Use and help evolve agentic AI tools to support IP workflows such as docketing, disclosure intake, prior art gathering, and portfolio reporting, and bring ideas for where automation can meaningfully improve program efficiency. Qualifications Need to have: - A sense of humor and a team mindset - 10+ years of experience as an IP paralegal, with a mix of in-house and law firm experience - Demonstrated AI tool fluency and genuine curiosity about applying agentic AI systems to IP program operations - Hands-on experience supporting a mix of patent and trademark prosecution workflows, including docketing, filing coordination, and portfolio maintenance - Working knowledge of copyright administration and trade secret protection practices - Experience managing outside counsel relationships, including invoice review, budget tracking, and adherence to outside counsel guidelines - Experience managing a high volume of concurrent matters and deadlines with strong organizational skills and exacting attention to detail - Ability to multitask and effectively manage competing priorities in a fast-paced startup environment - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to correspond directly with outside counsel, inventors, and internal stakeholders - Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential and privileged material - Genuine interest in IP diligence work and in stepping into IP-adjacent needs as they come up, including commercial and litigation support Nice to have: - Paralegal certificate, associate's degree in paralegal studies, or bachelor's degree - Direct experience with open source license compliance review - Experience running or supporting an inventor recognition or patent rewards/incentive program - Experience supporting IP diligence for M&A, financing, or commercial transactions - Litigation support experience (e.g., discovery, document review, case file management) - Experience with IP portfolio analytics, competitive filing intelligence, or landscape mapping - Direct experience with docketing platforms, IP management software, and legal billing or matter management systems - Experience at a high-growth technology startup - Interest in artificial intelligence laws and regulations

items.title: Engineering Manager, Integrity and Attestation
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About Anthropic Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the team The Integrity and Attestation team's remit is to prove what is running at Anthropic: what code it is, where it came from, and whether the machine underneath it is in a known-good state. We build the systems that cryptographically verify build artifacts, model weights, and machines, from hardware roots of trust through firmware and boot to the credentials a workload receives. We also secure the management plane of our servers. These controls protect our model weights and customer data across cloud providers and bare-metal AI data centers, including sites operated by partners. We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead this team. Anthropic is bringing up new compute quickly, across new hardware platforms and new partners, and each one has to meet the same bar. In this role you will set the team's charter, practices, and priorities. You will partner with our infrastructure, data center, and hardware teams, as well as outside vendors, so that integrity is designed in rather than added later. The goal is simple to state: a machine gets secrets and workloads only after it proves it should, and a new site reaches that bar without slowing down compute. About the role Own the integrity roadmap: threat model from silicon and firmware up through the operating system and workloads, decide what to build, and deliver it Be able to reason about the design and implementation of remote attestation, measured and verified boot, hardware roots of trust (TPM, SPDM), machine identity, and the reference values that define known-good Make attestation the default path, so machines receive credentials and join clusters only after proving their firmware, system software, and security configuration, with no human in the loop Build provenance for what we deploy: signed build artifacts and model weights, independent verification, and tamper-evident transparency logs Lead the protection of sensitive data in use and at rest, including encryption and the chokepoints that control access to it Secure the server management plane across every site: scoped and audited access to baseboard management controllers and management of per-device credentials Make security repeatable as compute grows, so a new site or hardware platform inherits these controls in hours, not weeks Join compute bring-up, data center, and hardware teams at design time Define clear ownership with partner teams: when operations move to another team, your team keeps the security properties and can prove they still hold Own the integrity evidence for our security goals and compliance: the invariants hold, and you can prove it Hire, grow, and retain senior security software engineers; own their career development, and set the practices the team runs on as it scales Who you are Low ego, high empathy; has built diverse teams and has former reports who would vouch for them. Experience managing infrastructure or security engineering teams, including hiring, developing, and managing senior and staff engineers Has grown engineers into staff or lead roles, and experience with performance management Created and maintained a high performing in hypergrowth environments. Kept a team intact and delivering through reorgs, charter changes, or leadership turnover Experience owning a security or infrastructure domain end to end: setting multi-year strategy, delivering year-long cross-organizational work with little direction, and answering to executives for its risk and tradeoffs An appreciation for distributed systems and properties beyond security, including reliability, efficiency, and maintainability Scaled a team and its systems together through hypergrowth, where last quarter's architecture was already too small Hands-on engineering in at least one of: platform security, secure boot and firmware, hardware roots of trust, confidential computing, or software supply chain integrity Threat modeling and risk assessment for systems that span hardware and software, with strong security judgment and pragmatism Comfortable leading through ambiguity with multiple partner teams and outside vendors, where you don't control the hardware or the schedule You may be a good fit if you have: At least 5+ years managing engineering teams and 8+ years hands-on in platform, infrastructure, or security engineering Built or operated remote attestation, device identity, or fleet-wide boot integrity at production scale Worked with BMCs, Redfish, GPU or accelerator attestation, or large-scale bare-metal provisioning Experience with Nitro, SEV-SNP, TDX, or similar confidential computing platforms Built signing, provenance, or transparency systems such as Sigstore, SLSA, or binary transparency Designed key management or offline ceremonies for high-value secrets Worked in high-assurance environments where controls had to be evidenced, not just deployed Taken infrastructure from zero to one and then to maturity: built the first version where nothing existed, then run and hardened it into a system other teams depend on Built or rebuilt a hiring loop and held the bar while adding headcount quickly Pragmatic and steady: cares about unblocking research, product and compute as much as a clean architecture, and brings patience and judgment to opinionated senior engineers Clear and persuasive communicator in writing and in person Familiarity with AI security and safety concepts The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Customer Support Specialist II you will serve as a primary subject matter expert for Coinbase’s products, providing world-class service and support to our most valued customers. You’ll join a team of customer focused support professionals who know their performance is essential to Coinbase achieving its mission. We’re looking for an individual who has a passion for making the customer experience seamless and phenomenal. What you’ll be doing (ie. job duties): Responsible for providing support for high-profile Coinbase customers across multiple channels (phone, messaging & email) by investigating, troubleshooting and resolving customer issues. Use all available resources to ensure high standards are met and work is carried out in the most efficient manner. Be a trusted advisor, listen and empathize so the customer knows they are valued. Ensure their voices are heard through accurate issue tracking and upstream solutions. Take ownership and use critical thinking to find the root cause and solve the customer issue on the first contact. Where this is not possible, ensure all defects are logged appropriately. Seek opportunities to add value for customers through education, proactivity and clear expectation setting. You will be responsible for providing best in class customer support, handling customers proactively to mitigate issues, handling contacts through to resolution, and collaborating across teams of subject matter specialists to fix issues with urgency. Model an investigative mentality: utilize data and customer feedback to help address critical customer issues at the root cause and eliminate defects in the customer experience. Proactively identify customer needs before they become an issue to simplify the customer experience, reduce friction, and strengthen trust in Coinbase. Champion clear communication with internal and external partners to align on solutions and drive results. Develop a deep understanding of Coinbase products and ongoing changes in the macro crypto environment so you can guide customers to navigate the quickly moving and ever changing crypto world and unlock additional features, services, and products that benefit their unique profile. What we look for in you (ie. job requirements): This role requires full-time, in-office presence, five days a week. Willingness to work nights and weekends to support the 24/7 nature of cryptocurrency markets. Motivated by Coinbase’s mission and creating a seamless experience for our highest value customers. Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in a customer service or support role in a fast paced environment including working with high value customers. Basic knowledge of blockchain, web3, staking, ROI/staking rewards, self-custody, and/or crypto. Flexible and adaptable to meet the evolving needs of a high-growth and fast paced organization. Fantastic communication and relationship management skills, passion for assisting customers to use Coinbase products successfully, and an eagerness to create a community of high value Coinbase power users. Nice to haves: Experience at crypto exchanges or in financial services, ideally in payments, trading operations or technical support. You’ll bring a clear view of delivery progress, risks, and expected outcomes, helping teams make informed decisions and connecting successful execution to consumption and growth. This is a senior, customer-facing role for someone who can move between executive conversations and practical details that determine whether a deployment succeeds. You bring technical fluency, sound judgment, and the ability to create clarity and drive action in complex, evolving environments. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own delivery of priority AI initiatives. items.title: Product Growth
items.description: About the Team The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows. The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements. We combine product strategy, product experimentation, with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets. About the Role We’re looking for a hands-on Product Growth generalist with an international focus to help people get lasting value from ChatGPT across markets, use cases and product experiences. You’ll partner with international and central teams to understand user needs, identify growth opportunities and turn them into measurable improvements across acquisition, activation, engagement, retention and monetization. You’ll combine strong analytics and experimentation with product intuition, design judgment and a deep understanding of users and local markets. You’ll use AI-native automation and agentic tools to accelerate research, analysis, prototyping and execution. This role requires systems thinking and the ability to move across diverse experiences, improving both individual funnels and end-to-end workflows as products, user behavior and market needs evolve. You’ll be responsible for: - Partner with product, eng, and design to turn insights into intuitive experiences and prototypes, improving how users discover value, complete tasks and return. - Diagnose and optimize funnel performance using user research, event-level behavior, cohort analysis, and competitive insight. Identify drop-offs and high-value segments, distinguish local needs from shared product friction, and prioritize interventions. - Build and use agentic workflows to automate research, analysis, prototyping and experiment operations, with clear quality checks and human judgment where needed. - Connect acquisition and marketing insights to product journeys; partner with regional marketers and channel specialists on tests that improve qualified acquisition and activation. - Own a rigorous experimentation program across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, paid conversion, and expansion. Partner with Engineering and Data Science on hypotheses, instrumentation, A/B tests and holdouts, readouts, and staged rollouts, with clear success metrics and guardrails. - Build and execute a focused international growth roadmap, including in-product upsell, cross-sell, targeting, onboarding, activation/adoption, expansion, and monetization related experiences. Identify the use cases, onboarding barriers, product entry points, and upgrade moments that can improve adoption and sustained customer value. - Partner with Data Science and Engineering to develop, deploy, and improve classifiers and propensity models for segmentation, targeting, and personalized in-product journeys. Evaluate predictive quality and use controlled experiments to establish incremental activation, conversion, or expansion impact. - Own measurement across activation, retention, paid conversion, upsell, cross-sell, and revenue. Separate incremental impact from market mix, seasonality, or cannibalization, and use the results to decide what to scale, adapt, or stop. - Run a clear operating cadence with regional and central partners, surfacing international experimentation results, trade-offs, dependencies, and decisions without requiring formal ownership of every team involved. - Build repeatable growth primitives, such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, referral and expansion triggers, and experimentation tooling, that can be reused across segments and markets. Use AI-native workflows to accelerate research, prototyping, and iteration. We’re looking for someone with: - Experience across product growth, growth strategy and operations, data science, experimentation, and growth design systems, with hands-on ownership of product experiments and measurable outcomes in a fast-moving technology company. - A user-first track record of translating research and behavior into product priorities, then working with technical teams to ship improvements. - Deep expertise in funnel optimization and experimentation, including instrumentation, A/B testing, statistical power, holdouts, segmentation, cohort analysis, and interpreting incremental impact. A track record of turning experiment results into sustained product improvements. - The ability to work across product and marketing levers, connecting audience and acquisition insights to activation, retention, and monetization. - Analytical fluency in funnel modeling and growth economics, including incrementality, LTV, CAC, and payback; the ability to move between strategic prioritization and hands-on execution. - Practical experience applying classifiers and propensity models to growth problems with Data Science and Engineering, including choosing useful signals, evaluating model quality, and testing the impact of targeted interventions. - Ideally, experience scaling and continuously optimizing growth initiatives within Engineering and Data Science pods, from shared prioritization and implementation through experimentation and rollout. - Experience adapting products or growth programs across markets, with sound judgment about language, local behavior, business needs, and what should remain consistent globally. - Experience optimizing self-serve funnels and in-product upsell, cross-sell, or expansion journeys, or strong evidence of applying comparable growth expertise to a new customer segment/goal - The ability to influence central and regional teams, work independently through ambiguity, and carry an initiative from diagnosis through execution and evaluation. items.title: Lead Counsel, Commercial (Energy - Infrastructure)
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Legal team plays a crucial role in advancing our mission by tackling innovative and fundamental legal issues in AI. The team includes professionals from diverse legal fields—technology, AI, infrastructure, privacy, IP, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation—who collaborate closely with colleagues across the company. If you are passionate about being an energy and infrastructure lawyer working on cutting-edge challenges, you’ll thrive here. About the Role We’re seeking an experienced energy lawyer to support the business on legal matters relating to the energy and power infrastructure supporting OpenAI’s fast-growing data center portfolio. This is a cross-functional role that will partner closely with energy, infrastructure development, engineering, procurement, and finance teams to advise on complex legal and regulatory issues and help structure, negotiate, and manage the transactions that secure reliable, cost-effective power for OpenAI’s long-term infrastructure ambitions. We’re looking for an experienced energy and infrastructure lawyer who thrives in ambiguity and wants to help define the commercial playbook for power procurement and energy project development in the AI era. This role reports to the Associate General Counsel for Infrastructure. The role’s scope and level will reflect the successful candidate’s experience and expertise. In this role, you will: - Own legal strategy and risk management for OpenAI’s global energy procurement and power infrastructure transactions, from initial structuring through execution and ongoing implementation. - Draft, negotiate, and advise on complex power purchase agreements, energy supply and hedging arrangements, and utility service and special contracts, including related regulatory requirements and approvals. - Structure and negotiate interconnection, transmission, and utility infrastructure arrangements that align power availability with data center development and operating schedules. - Advise leadership and business leaders on legal and regulatory considerations as they develop and implement our energy and data center strategy - Support strategic partnerships involving renewable and other carbon-free generation, energy storage, and on-site or behind-the-meter power solutions for AI infrastructure. - Develop legal and regulatory frameworks for energy procurement, project development, and collaboration with utilities, independent power producers, and energy developers. - Partner with finance and operations teams to align contract terms with business and compliance requirements, including pricing, delivery and curtailment risk, credit support, and project milestones. - Collaborate with policy and regulatory colleagues on issues impacting energy transactions, utility tariffs, grid access, market participation, retail service requirements, and renewable energy attributes. - Build scalable, efficient contracting processes that support OpenAI’s energy and infrastructure development at speed while managing legal and regulatory risk. - Guide outside counsel and coordinate with real estate, construction, tax, and regulatory counsel on energy transactions and project development. You might thrive in this role if you: - 10+ years of legal experience, with substantial focus on complex commercial energy transactions. - Have a JD and license or qualification to practice in CA. - Relevant experience in-house, at a law firm, or a combination of both, advising energy companies, utilities, developers, major power customers, or infrastructure investors. - Demonstrated experience independently leading complex energy transactions, including power purchase, utility service, or interconnection agreements. - Familiarity with U.S. electricity markets, utility tariffs, and the regulatory frameworks affecting energy supply, interconnection, and transmission, including FERC, state utility commissions, and regional grid operators. - Strong commercial judgment and financial fluency in energy pricing, volume commitments, credit support, and allocation of development and operating risk. - Demonstrated ability to operate with autonomy and sound judgment in highly technical and fast-moving environments. - Exceptional communication skills, with an ability to distill complexity into actionable, business-aligned guidance and advise senior business leaders on strategic decisions. - Experience advising on cross-border energy deals and international energy regulatory frameworks is a plus. - Prior experience with data center power procurement, generation or storage development, energy project finance, joint ventures, or on-site and behind-the-meter energy projects is a strong plus. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. items.title: Content Strategy Lead, Executive Programs
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As the Content Strategy Lead for Executive Programs, you will own what Anthropic brings to the table when we sit down with senior leaders from our most strategic customers. That covers Executive Briefings, Customer Advisory Boards, Executive Councils, and the other small-room gatherings where a C-level audience meets with our leaders, product teams, and researchers. You will set the content strategy across these programs, build the library of modules and the bench of speakers, and lead the team that keeps our content fresh as our models and products evolve. This role works cross-functionally with Product & Solutions Marketing, who owns positioning and messaging across industries and products, and customer programs which owns each program's operations, intake, and customer experience. You own the layer in between: turning Anthropic's product, research, and policy story into sessions built for an executive audience, deciding who is best placed to deliver them, and designing interactive formats and demos that work for customers building on the frontier. The right candidate has a product marketing or narrative background, has built content for C-level customer audiences at an enterprise technology company, and has managed a team. Key responsibilities Set and execute the content strategy across Executive Briefings, Customer Advisory Boards, Executive Councils, and other gatherings of strategic customers: the themes for the year, the narrative that connects them, and how content differs by program, audience, and purpose. Build and maintain an evergreen library of content modules that program leads and account teams can assemble into an agenda without starting from scratch. Modules span product and roadmap, research, safety and policy, industry and use-case sessions, demos, and discussion guides. Keep the library current. Set a refresh cadence tied to model and product launches, retire what is stale, maintain a pipeline of net-new content modules, and make sure nothing in front of a customer executive is out of date. Identify, recruit, develop and certify speakers from Anthropic's executive, product, research, and go-to-market teams. Maintain the cross-program roster, shape each speaker's session, and prepare them for the room. Design the experience, not only the presentation. Choose the format that fits the audience and the goal, whether that is a working session, a live demo, a conversation with a researcher, or a peer discussion among customers. Partner with program leads on agendas for the highest-priority engagements, tailoring modules to the customer's objectives. Set the standards and templates that let every other engagement meet the same bar. Work with Product & Solutions Marketing, Product, and Research so that executive-level content is ready when a launch happens, not weeks after. Capture what customers say in these rooms, including themes, objections, and requests. Route it to Product, Research, Marketing, and go-to-market leadership, and use it to improve the content. Measure what works, including session feedback, module usage, and speaker performance, and work with program leads to connect content to program outcomes. Hire, manage, and develop the team responsible for executive program content, and set its quality bar. Use Claude to scale the work: build workflows that tailor modules to a customer's industry and priorities so a customized session does not require a rebuild. Minimum qualifications Built content for C-level customer audiences in executive briefings, advisory boards, executive councils, or similar programs. Built a content system that other people rely on, such as a module library, a session catalog, or a speaker program, and kept it current through frequent product change. The technical fluency to work directly with researchers and engineers, understand what they have built, and explain it accurately to a business executive. Experience coaching senior executives and technical experts as speakers, including giving direct feedback on their material. Judgment about format: you know when a room needs a presentation, a demo, or a facilitated discussion, and you can design each one. Experience managing people, including hiring and developing a team. A high bar for writing. You can draft an executive session narrative yourself and improve one written by someone else. Genuine interest in AI and in helping the world's largest enterprises adopt it responsibly. Preferred qualifications 12+ years in product marketing, executive content, or executive customer programs at a B2B technology company. You have owned positioning and messaging for a technical product and know how to adapt it for different audiences. Experience at a company where the product changes quickly and content has a short shelf life. Hands-on experience using AI tools to produce or tailor content. Experience facilitating executive discussions, not only preparing others to lead them. Worked with customers in regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or the public sector. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $400,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Customer Success, EMEA
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a Customer Success Manager (CSM) at Mistral, you will be responsible for managing a portfolio of enterprise customers, ensuring they achieve their goals using Mistral’s solutions. You will serve as the primary point of contact for customers, driving adoption, satisfaction, and long-term success. This role is ideal for those who excel in customer-facing environments, enjoy solving complex challenges, and are passionate about turning customer success into business impact. WHAT YOU WILL DO CUSTOMER SUCCESS OWNERSHIP - Manage a portfolio of enterprise customers, ensuring they maximize the value of Mistral’s AI solutions. - Build strong, trusted relationships with key stakeholders, understanding their business objectives and tailoring solutions to meet their needs. - Lead customer onboarding, adoption, and ongoing engagement to drive product usage and satisfaction. - Monitor customer health metrics, identify risks, and proactively address challenges to prevent churn. - Collaborate with Sales to identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities based on customer needs and usage patterns. - Partner with Product and Engineering teams to gather customer feedback and influence the product roadmap. - Develop and deliver customer training, enablement programs, and best practices to drive adoption. - Conduct regular business reviews (QBRs) to align on goals, challenges, and success metrics. STRATEGIC CUSTOMER GUIDANCE - Serve as a trusted advisor to customers, guiding them on how to leverage Mistral’s AI solutions to achieve their business outcomes. - Work closely with Support and Product teams to ensure seamless customer experiences, from deployment to production. - Create and execute customer success plans with clear KPIs, timelines, and measurable outcomes. - Advocate for customer needs internally, ensuring their voice is heard in product and strategic discussions. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION - Share customer insights with Product, Sales, and Engineering teams to inform product improvements and strategic initiatives. - Clear obstacles for customers during deployment and adoption phases, accelerating time-to-value. - Support renewal processes, including contract negotiations, expansion discussions, and coordination with internal teams. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 5+ years of experience in customer-facing roles, such as Customer Success, Account Management, or Solutions Consulting, ideally in a technical or SaaS environment. - Proven ability to manage enterprise customer relationships, with a focus on driving adoption, satisfaction, and retention. - Experience working with technical products, with the ability to engage confidently with Data, IT, and Engineering teams. - Strong communication and presentation skills, including the ability to tailor messaging for technical and executive audiences. - Business acumen: Ability to identify upsell and expansion opportunities while ensuring customer success. - Technical aptitude: Familiarity with AI/ML concepts is a plus; ability to understand and discuss technical requirements is essential. - Hands-on, customer-centric, collaborative, and organized, with a passion for solving complex challenges. items.description: About the Team Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models. We work across research, engineering, product, and policy to understand risks, develop and validate safeguards, and support responsible deployment. Our work spans safeguards research and deployment, safety assessments, launch readiness, and trusted-access programs for advanced capabilities. We address risks including biological and cyber misuse and misalignment, with programs that strengthen safety across models and products. About the Role We’re hiring Research Program Managers across AI Safeguards and Frontier Risks Safety. You’ll lead programs that develop and improve the safeguards used across our models and products, or assess and mitigate risks associated with frontier capabilities, launches, and trusted-access programs. You will partner with researchers, engineers, and other stakeholders to turn open safety questions into clear programs of work. You’ll shape technical roadmaps, coordinate execution, and use evidence to guide priorities and inform development and deployment decisions. We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience managing complex research programs, and a commitment to AI safety. These roles are based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Shape safety programs and technical roadmaps. Partner with research and engineering leads to define goals, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria. Prioritize intake and emerging findings, resolve blockers, and balance immediate safety needs with longer-term research and platform investments. - Drive safeguards development and deployment. Translate safety research into safeguards across models and products. Maintain an end-to-end view of safeguard coverage, effectiveness, and opportunities for improvement for one or more risk areas, and drive a roadmap that advances across launches. - Coordinate evaluations and safety assessments. Organize capability evaluations, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including risks from autonomous and multi-agent systems. Support embedded assessments throughout model development, internal use, and deployment. - Drive safety readiness and trusted-access programs. Coordinate safety requirements and execution across frontier model launches and deployments. Work with technical teams to define assessment scope and the evidence needed to inform safety and access decisions. - Turn findings into improvements. Triage safeguard gaps, jailbreaks, and overflagging with accountable teams. Establish owners and escalation paths, track remediation and regression testing, and turn recurring issues into research and engineering improvements. - Strengthen the evidence behind safety decisions. Support safety cases that connect claims to evaluations, safeguards, assumptions, and remaining uncertainty. Surface evidence gaps and unresolved risks, and communicate methods, results, limitations, and follow-up actions through assessment reports, system cards, and updates to decision-makers. - Build programs that scale across products. Coordinate shared tooling and feedback workflows, privacy and security requirements, and safeguard user experience and quality assurance. Help teams apply safeguards consistently across product surfaces and upcoming launches. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 5+ years of experience in technical safety work, owning technical programs, or related roles in fast-moving environments. - Have led complex research or technical programs involving researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences. - Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evaluations, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams. - Can assess what evaluation results do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and the difference between model capability and real-world risk. - Can turn ambiguous questions into clear programs, make practical tradeoffs, and adjust priorities as evidence changes. - Have worked extensively across research, engineering, and product teams and can coordinate with policy and communications partners. - Exercise sound judgment when findings are concerning or incomplete, raise unresolved risks constructively, and communicate complex technical work clearly. - Are motivated to help ensure increasingly capable AI systems remain beneficial and under meaningful human control. items.title: Sales Enablement Operations Manager
items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), Austin, New York City
items.description: Perplexity's sales organization is growing fast, and our sellers need the right content, tools and AI workflows to win. As our first Sales Enablement Operations Manager, you'll be the strategic partner and builder behind how Perplexity's sales team finds, uses and learns from content. This role is both strategic and hands-on. You'll work with the Sales Enablement Lead to define our content management strategy, including whether to build on Perplexity's own AI platform or buy a dedicated tool. Then you'll build it, run it and keep improving it. You'll also build AI skills, plugins and workflows that make reps and managers faster and more effective every day. This is a foundational hire. We're looking for someone who can grow into a leadership role as the enablement function scales. RESPONSIBILITIES Help shape content and knowledge strategy - Partner with the Sales Enablement Lead to define the long-term content management strategy for the sales team, from requirements to the build-vs-buy decision. - Work alongside the Sales Enablement Lead on the evaluation: gather stakeholder needs, assess options (including Perplexity Computer and third-party platforms), model costs and tradeoffs, and shape a joint recommendation to sales leadership. - Design the content architecture: taxonomy, ownership, governance, approval workflows and lifecycle (create, review, update, retire). Help build and run the enablement stack - Own the implementation and maintenance of the sales content hub, call library and training platform, leveraging Perplexity throughout. - Help coordinate with Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, Product and Legal so content is accurate, approved and available where sellers work (Salesforce, Slack, call-recording tools). - Own enablement reporting: content usage, training completion, certification status and how they relate to ramp and performance. Build AI tools for the sales team - Design, build and maintain AI skills, plugins and agent workflows for account executives, BDRs and sales managers, such as account research, call prep, deal reviews, coaching and pipeline hygiene. - Turn repeated seller and manager tasks into reusable AI workflows, then drive adoption through training, documentation and feedback loops. - Develop training materials for sellers and managers on using AI tools well, and keep a shared library of best practices. Lead and scale - Set the standards for how enablement content and AI tools get built, contributed and maintained across the GTM organization. - Act as a trusted thought partner to enablement leadership on priorities, operating model and tooling. - Help shape the enablement operations function as the team grows, with a path to leading it. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 4–6 years in go-to-market roles, with at least 2 years owning sales enablement operations, revenue operations, GTM systems or sales content strategy. - Experience owning a sales content or knowledge system end to end, including taxonomy, governance, adoption and measurement. - A track record of leading or heavily shaping a tooling decision, such as a platform evaluation, migration or in-house build. - Real, hands-on AI fluency: you've built AI tools or workflows (custom GPTs, Claude or Perplexity skills, MCP connectors, n8n, Zapier, Clay or similar) that other people use regularly, and you can show examples. - Systems thinking: you understand how content, CRM, call-recording and communication tools connect, and you design for how sellers actually work. - Strong judgment and the ability to make a clear recommendation and defend it with leadership. - Experience driving cross-functional projects without formal authority. - Clear written and verbal communication, and a bias toward shipping, measuring and iterating. Nice to have - Experience as the first enablement operations or GTM systems hire, building the function from scratch. - Hands-on experience with enablement platforms such as Highspot, Seismic, Guru, Mindtickle or Showpad. - Background as an AE, SE or BDR before moving into enablement or operations. - Experience managing or mentoring contractors, interns or direct reports. - Experience at a high-growth AI or SaaS company. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE - First 90 days: You've assessed current content and tools, interviewed sellers and managers, made a build-vs-buy recommendation with the Sales Enablement Lead, and shipped the first AI skills the sales team uses every week. - First 6 months: A governed content hub and call library are live and adopted, enablement reporting is in place, and a growing library of AI tools is measurably saving time for reps and managers. - First year: Enablement operations is a scalable function with clear standards, and you're ready to lead it as the team grows.

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry. At the scale we build, our campuses are typically served by dedicated high-voltage substations and a medium-voltage distribution network that may also integrate on-site generation and battery energy storage — and the protection, control, and automation layer is what keeps all of it selective, coordinated, and observable. As a Data Center Substation, Protection & Automation Engineer, you'll own the protection and automation architecture across Anthropic's US portfolio — from the utility point of interconnection (POI) through the HV/MV substation, the MV distribution loop, and down into LV switchgear. protection settings that satisfy ride-through and grid-code requirements Review the protection and control interface for on-site generation and battery energy storage interconnections, including anti-islanding, synchronizing, and intertie protection Support NERC PRC compliance for applicable facilities — settings documentation, misoperation analysis, and periodic maintenance and testing basis Testing, commissioning & standards Develop relay test plans and factory and site acceptance test procedures for protection and automation systems, and witness FAT, relay secondary-injection testing, GOOSE messaging and end-to-end scheme testing, and integrated systems testing Review the protection and control steps of energization and switching methods of procedure (MOPs), support first-energization of substations and MV distribution, and resolve protection and control issues found in the field Lead root-cause analysis of protection operations and misoperations using relay event records, sequence-of-events data, and disturbance records, and feed findings back into settings and standards Build and continuously improve Anthropic's internal protection and automation standards — settings templates, scheme logic libraries, test procedures, and commissioning checklists — so each new site starts from a proven baseline You may be a good fit if you Have 10+ years of experience in power system protection engineering, substation automation, or substation design for utility, heavy-industrial, or mission-critical facilities Hold a bachelor's degree in Electrical protective relays for transformers, feeders, buses, generators, and switchgear, and are fluent in at least one major relay platform (e.g., SEL, GE Multilin, ABB, Siemens) Are fluent in short-circuit, protective-device coordination, and arc-flash analysis and comfortable running or critically reviewing studies in tools such as SKM, ETAP, EasyPower, ASPEN, or CAPE Have hands-on experience integrating protective relays into substation automation or SCADA systems using protocols such as DNP3, Modbus, or IEC 61850, and understand RTU/gateway and sequence-of-events architecture Have worked The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI). As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is. items.title: Talent Sourcer, G&A
items.location_text: New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Toronto
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? Cohere is in a unique and exciting position to grow our go-to-market teams globally! We are expanding our Talent Team and are looking for creative, high-performing talent sourcers who are eager to take on a new challenge as we are in the early stages of building the Talent Acquisition function. In this role, you will master a new domain of sourcing, source world-class business talent, and influence the scaling of a high-growth Canadian tech company. If you consider yourself resilient, collaborative, influential, and a lifelong learner with an established network, we’d love to hear from you! In this intermediate level role you will: - Build, own, and nurture a strong pipeline of world-class business talent across Sales, Finance, Revenue, Marketing & Communications, and Operations - Deliver a world-class recruiting experience that reflects Cohere's premium brand - Partner with hiring managers and talent partners to find and engage passive talent through creative sourcing methods - Maintain deep market intelligence on business talent trends and competitive landscape - Manage comprehensive recruiting funnels in our ATS, updating progress and analytics regularly - Develop creative, proactive sourcing approaches to optimize the top of the funnel for business roles - Cultivate relationships with established networks across business communities and industry leaders - Identify and own additional high-impact talent projects as they emerge Who you are: - You have 3 -7 years of experience sourcing for business roles across Sales, Finance, Revenue, Marketing & Communications, and Operations in markets like EMEA/US etc. - You have a proven track record of sourcing candidates in high-growth and a high-bar environments (startup, technology, AI experience strongly preferred) - You bring an established, high-profile network in business communities - You're a creative problem solver who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments - You're a natural influencer with exceptional relationship-building skills - You leverage data and analytics to drive sourcing decisions and measure effectiveness - You're passionate about diversity, equity, and building inclusive business teams - You have a strategic mindset with the ability to see beyond immediate hiring needs WHY COHERE - Impact: Shape the future of AI talent at a cutting-edge company. - Culture: Collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven. - Growth: Join a team scaling from 800 to 2000+ over 18 months. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.title: Quant Risk Analyst - Derivatives & Clearing
items.description: About Polymarket Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform, where people trade on the outcomes of real-world events. As our markets, volumes, and derivative product suite grow, so does the sophistication of the risk infrastructure behind them. Our clearing and risk systems must operate with the rigor of a traditional clearinghouse while moving at the speed of a crypto-native trading platform. The Role We're hiring a mid-level quantitative risk analyst to design and implement enterprise-scale risk models at the heart of our clearing operation. You'll own models for market risk, volatility and correlation of derivatives, stress testing, and automated liquidation — the systems that keep the platform solvent and users protected in fast-moving markets. This is a hands-on role: you'll be building models in production code, not just specifying them. We expect you to work fluently with AI tools for development and research — and to be the skeptic in the room, pressure-testing AI-generated models and code against well-established risk frameworks before anything ships. What You'll Do - Design, implement, and maintain enterprise-scale risk models covering market risk, margin, and counterparty exposure for a clearing organization. - Build volatility and correlation models for derivatives, including calibration, backtesting, and ongoing model validation. - Develop and run stress-testing frameworks: historical scenarios, hypothetical shocks, and reverse stress tests. - Design and tune auto-liquidation logic — trigger thresholds, liquidation waterfalls, and safeguards against cascading liquidations. - Use AI tools extensively to accelerate model development, coding, and research — and rigorously validate AI outputs against established risk models (VaR/ES, SPAN-style margining, GARCH-family volatility models, standard correlation frameworks) before deployment. - Monitor model performance in production, investigate breaks, and iterate quickly. - Partner with engineering, trading, and product teams to embed risk controls into platform architecture. - Document model assumptions, limitations, and validation results to an audit-ready standard. What We're Looking For - 5–7 years of quantitative risk experience at a clearinghouse, exchange, prime broker, trading firm, or similar. - Proven expertise designing and implementing risk models at enterprise scale — production systems, not just research prototypes. - Deep experience modeling volatility, correlation, option skews, option pricing and implementing at scale for trad-fi derivatives, perpetuals, and fully collateralized event contracts. - Hands-on experience with market risk modeling, stress testing, and auto-liquidation mechanics in a clearing context. - Strong fluency with AI-assisted development and coding, paired with the judgment to pressure-test AI outputs against well-established risk models and catch what looks plausible but is wrong. - Expert-level Python (numerical stack: NumPy, pandas, SciPy; solid software engineering practices). - Advanced degree in a quantitative field (math, statistics, physics, financial engineering, CS) or equivalent experience. - Strong mathematical foundation in stochastic calculus and linear algebra. Nice to Have - C# and/or C++ for performance-critical or production systems. - Familiarity with crypto market structure, perpetuals, or prediction markets. - Experience with CCP risk frameworks (CPMI-IOSCO PFMI, default management, margin methodology). - Experience building real-time risk systems. Location & Work Setup This role is based in our New York City office, in person. You'll be working directly alongside the trading, engineering, and risk teams.
